engine: Remotion render (Chromium headless shell, SwiftShader) launched by a codex exec subagent
environment: codex exec -s workspace-write (DeepSeek V4.1 builder, task T-V07m master-4k-v001), Windows 11
symptom: Inside the codex workspace-write sandbox, Remotion could not render: first `spawn EPERM` (esbuild loader, where.exe, ffprobe, chrome-headless-shell.exe), then after workarounds Chromium died with `FATAL mojo platform_channel.cc:112 Check failed: Access is denied (0x5)` and `Failed to grant sandbox access to cache directory`. The builder burned time on loader/browser hacks (jsx-loader-no-child.cjs, connected-browser path).
root_cause: The codex Windows sandbox runs commands under a restricted token that forbids child-process creation and Chromium's own sandbox/IPC channel. It is a policy of the sandbox, not a broken install; restarting the agent does not change it. A web-scraping MCP (Firecrawl) cannot render local Remotion compositions either.
fix_or_workaround: Root (unsandboxed host shell) runs every Remotion/Chromium/ffmpeg-spawning render; codex subagents only prepare configs/scripts. For T-V07m root ran `node editorial/master-4k-v001/render_master_v001.cjs --preview --stills ...` at below-normal priority.
prevention: Never delegate a Remotion/Chromium render to a codex exec sandboxed subagent (Gemini/DeepSeek route); give them config/script work and state 'root renders'. Claude Agent-tool subagents running in the host shell may render (CPU, concurrency <= 2).
verification: D6-deepseek-codex.jsonl log lines (EPERM, mojo 0x5); root render result recorded in PLAN T-V07m.
